metadata.scenario_context: Several multinational companies are collaborating on a project and have decided to hold a joint meeting in early November to determine progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China disagree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Russia agree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss proposing to hold the meeting on the first Tuesday of November.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss the appropriateness of government actions.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to discuss government actions.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Hi Kim, have we decided on a date for the joint meeting in November? I think proposing the first Tuesday would work well for everyone. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Uh... the first Tuesday, you say? I guess that could be... okay. But, um, I think we should double-check with everyone else too, right? Make sure it fits everyone’s schedule.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Yeah, of course. It’s important to confirm with everyone. I just believe that starting on the first Tuesday could give us a strong kick-off. By the way, do you often talk about the appropriateness of government actions in your meetings?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Well, talking about government actions... it's not really common in my experience. People here... they tend to avoid it. It’s not like we have a say in it anyway. So, um, yeah, meetings usually focus more on work-related things.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I understand. It’s interesting how different cultures approach that. In my experience in China, discussing government actions isn't really an option either. It makes me curious, though—don’t you think it’s important for people to have a say in what the government does?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Hmm... important, sure. But in Russia, it’s complicated. We know the system doesn’t really allow us to have that say. It's just... frustrating, you know? Better to focus on things we can change—like our project meeting. Speaking of which, should we finalize that date?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Yes, let’s focus on what we can change. Finalizing the first Tuesday sounds good to me. I think it would set a positive tone for our project moving forward. Should I draft an email to confirm with everyone?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: You know, at the end of the day, it's all the same. People figure it out. I mean, we all have our own ways of handling things, right? I don't really see meaningful differences here. So, if we agree on the first Tuesday, I can draft a quick email to confirm that with everyone. Sounds good?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message: That sounds good. I appreciate you taking the lead on that. It's just... I think recognizing differences can help us understand each other better. But for now, let’s stick to finalizing the meeting. Thanks, Kim.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: Right... understanding is important, I guess. But let’s just keep our focus on the meeting and get that sorted. I’ll handle the email. Thanks for your input, Mike. GOOD BYE!
turns.label: Minimization
